method: Frames per foot is fixed by the gauge. 35 mm advances four perforations per frame at a 3/16 inch perforation pitch, so 64 perforations, or 16 frames, fill one foot; 3-perf and 2-perf layouts use the same 64-perforation foot and therefore 21 1/3 and 32 frames per foot. 16 mm advances 7.62 mm per frame, which gives 40 frames per foot, Super 8 gives 72 and regular 8 mm 80. The frame count is the footage multiplied by the frames per foot, rounded to the nearest whole frame with ties rounded up; a length that holds less than one whole frame of the chosen gauge is refused rather than reported as zero. Running time is the frame count divided by the camera frame rate, printed as hours, minutes, seconds and tenths, with hours omitted below an hour. Linear film speed is the frame rate divided by the frames per foot and multiplied by sixty, so 4-perf 35 mm at 24 frames per second moves 90 feet of film past the gate each minute. Reels are the footage divided by the reel or magazine load, rounded up, and the final reel is reported with the footage it actually carries. The frame rates offered are 18, 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48 and 60 frames per second, and the constants are nominal: short and long perforation pitch, lab splices, leaders, edge numbers and the frames a camera loses when it starts and stops are not modelled, so a real camera report may run a frame or two either side. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Wikipedia, 35 mm movie film: the standard single-frame format is four perforations per frame, which gives 16 frames per foot, one frame is 3/4 inch at a 3/16 inch perforation pitch, and 24 frames per second runs 90 feet per minute with 1,000 feet about 11 minutes
Wikipedia, 16 mm film: the frame pitch is 7.62 mm for print stock, giving 40 frames per foot, and 400 feet runs about 11 minutes at 24 frames per second

Wikipedia, Super 8 film: a 50-foot cartridge holds 72 frames per foot for 3,600 frames, which is 2.5 minutes at 24 frames per second and 3.33 minutes at 18 frames per second, and standard 8 mm has a 0.1500 inch perforation pitch
